title: Twisted-Yetter downstream subject ontology v0

scope.question: Specify a first downstream twisted-yetter subject ontology to support search, disambiguation, and generated wiki views.
scope.claim_boundary: This note defines proposed twisted-yetter subject kinds and seed subjects. It does not assert new mathematical results, does not create a complete subject registry, and does not claim compatibility with any future ctl-meta subject profile.
scope.migration_expectation: If a future ctl-meta subject profile differs from this proposal, twisted-yetter should admit explicit migration operations preserving old ids and mapping them to the upstream-compatible form.

ontology_policy.display_name_policy: Display names are human-facing and may be corrected append-only. Subject ids should be stable.
ontology_policy.granularity_policy: Use the most precise subject available for claims and artifacts, while allowing broad hub subjects for discoverability.
ontology_policy.broad_subject_policy: Broad subjects such as Yasui or SU(2) should be hubs or family subjects. They should not be treated as if they were one paper, one diagram, or one MTC.
ontology_policy.prose_policy: Human wiki pages may be generated from these subjects, but project state must remain in admitted JSON artifacts and CTL objects.

proposed_subject_kinds.description: A human researcher or author relevant to sources, diagrams, or constructions.
A specific paper, preprint, book section, or source document.
A specific figure or diagram as it appears in a source.
A family of links or Kirby diagrams related by parameters or source presentation.
A specific link or surgery presentation, including normalization choices when relevant.
A smooth or topological four-manifold subject.
A family of tensor categories or MTCs, not necessarily one concrete category.
A classical Lie group as a mathematical input or background subject.
A concrete modular tensor category or category model used in computations.
Concrete F/R, fusion, S/T, or related category data artifact.
A reusable computational or theoretical route, such as separated character scan or non-separated Yasui evaluation.
A cluster of related claims or lab notes used as a human navigation hub.

seed_subjects.scope_note: Navigation hub for Yasui-related people, papers, figures, link families, and experiments. This subject must not be treated as one paper or one link.
The classical Lie group SU(2). It is not itself the same subject as the modular tensor category family SU(2)_k.
The level-k SU(2) modular tensor category family. Specific levels such as SU(2)_8 should be separate concrete MTC subjects.
Concrete SU(2) level 8 MTC subject. It should be linked to experiments only when that level was actually used.
Family of Drinfeld double categories, including twisted and untwisted finite-group examples. Concrete categories such as D(A4) omega0 and D(A4)c3w1 should be separate MTC subjects.
Untwisted Drinfeld double of A4 used in Yasui a=1 and a=3 computations.
H3 cocycle twisted D(A4) category with c3-inflated omega_power=1 on A4/V4 ~= C3.
Parameterized Yasui Figure 3 link family. The exact source paper and bibliographic reference should be attached by future reference records.
The normalized non-separated Yasui a=1 link presentation used in the July 2026 singleton computations.
Cheap ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar character-twist scan route. It mainly sees pointed/simple-current phase data and should not be mistaken for a non-separated Yasui computation.
Full sector-by-sector non-separated Yasui link evaluation route using category data and braid/link presentation.
Navigation cluster for the July 2026 Yasui a=1 baseline, D(A4)c3w1 component-A twist, separated character scans, and negative/positive candidate filters.

known_open_issues: The exact Yasui paper metadata and figure reference should be captured as repo-local reference records before creating precise ty:paper and ty:figure subjects.
The current seed subject for Yasui Figure 3 is provisional until source-paper metadata and diagram provenance are attached.
This note does not yet create actual subject-definition CTL revisions for each seed subject; it records a proposed ontology and seed plan.
No dedicated subject-layer verifier exists yet.
Future generated wiki pages must not become a second source of truth.
first_implementation_plan: Admit this ontology note and the design proposal note into CTL dogfood.
If accepted, add a small script that projects admitted subject-like JSON into a current subject index.
Create actual subject-definition JSON artifacts for the seed subjects only after the proposal is reviewed.
Attach subject edges to existing Yasui a=1 lab notes through explicit CTL objects or a later admitted subject-edge bundle.
